I’m using the `crimes-codebase-risk` workflow because this is a pre-edit investigation in a TypeScript/Python repo. I’ll run targeted `crimes context` checks on both sides of the boundary, then inspect the referenced files to distinguish the core rename from adjacent contract drift.

The repository-local skill path advertised for this checkout is not present at that relative location, so I’m resolving it from the supplied absolute locator before proceeding. No source files are being modified.

The first targeted invocation exposed a CLI path-resolution detail: when `--root` is set, `context` expects the file path relative to that root. I’m rerunning with `packages/...` paths; this is diagnostic only and did not alter the fixture.

The targeted contexts confirm the rename spans exactly three scanned source files and currently has no detected test coverage. I’m checking the literal identifiers, parameters, URLs, comments/docstrings, and return payloads now, because a safe rename must include wire-level strings—not just symbol names.

The core object is the product’s tenant/account container:

- Python calls it `team`.
- TypeScript calls it `workspace`.
- `crimes` recommends the shared name `organization`.

The rename spans three source files:

- [plans.py](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:11>) — “team” in the `Plan` docstring.
- [routes.py](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:10>) — `/api/teams` paths, `get_team`, `create_team`, `team_seats`, `change_team_plan`, and `team_id`.
- [workspace-client.ts](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:12>) — `Workspace`, all four exported function names, comments, return types, and `/api/workspaces`/`/api/teams` URLs.

A complete rename should therefore align both code identifiers and the HTTP contract, probably around `Organization` and `/api/organizations/{organization_id}`.

Other issues that should be handled or explicitly separated from the rename:

- High risk: the `Plan` closed sets disagree. Python has `free | pro | team | scale`; TypeScript has `free | pro | enterprise`. The `team` plan tier is distinct from the tenant object and should not be mechanically renamed.
- `changeWorkspacePlan` uses `PUT`, while the backend declares `POST`.
- The frontend’s `/api/workspaces` calls have no matching backend routes.
- The seats and plan calls contain literal `:id` instead of interpolating the supplied `id`.
- Renaming `getWorkspace` to `getOrganization` would retain the reported read-like-name/side-effect mismatch; `fetchOrganization` would better describe it.
- `crimes context` found no likely tests for any of the three files, so route/client contract tests should accompany the refactor.

The scan reported five findings: one high, three medium, and one low. Three JSON files and one TOML file were outside scan coverage; a literal repository search found no additional occurrences there. No changes were made.
